messages:
Alex Nguyen: Heads-up — after the prefetcher change pushed ~09:10 we see collector CPU p99 jump and span export p99 up ~120ms. spans/sec ~3x baseline.
Samir Patel: ugh. is this the new windowed prefetcher?
Alex Nguyen: yeah, config: `prefetch.batch_size=128`, `prefetch.window_ms=2000`, exporter flush_interval=250ms.
Riya Kapoor: alert from ingest-bot: `ingest:collector:cpu>80%` across 3 nodes at 09:12 :rotating_light:
ingest-bot: Alert: collector-cpu-high on prod-collector-{a,b,c} (firing)
Ben Ortiz: can you paste the flame or top callers? suspect GC/serialize churn from bigger batches.
Carla Mendes: grabbed a quick perf sample (10s): main hotspots -> `exporter::serialize_spans` and `prefetch::drain_loop`. flame: https://grafana.company/internal/flows/fg123 (private)
Alex Nguyen: repro commands I ran: ```kubectl exec -it collector-0 -- bash -c "tcpdump -nni lo port 4317"``` and `kubectl logs collector-0 -c collector | grep 'prefetch'` showed repeated `drain_time=15ms` becoming `drain_time=120ms`
Samir Patel: interesting — drain_time ramping suggests backpressure into exporter or blocking in serialization. try reducing `batch_size` to 32 and increase `flush_interval` to 1000ms as an experiment. smaller batches -> less serialization spike.
Riya Kapoor: also check retention/eviction churn: if TTL sweep runs while prefetch is large, extra allocs. Ben, any mem/alloc traces?
Ben Ortiz: memory steady but alloc rate spikes. suspect temporary vector growth while building protobuf buffers for 128 spans. quick mitigation: enable span-level sampling on ingest route for noisy clients (e.g., svg-renderer) and turn on `span_drop.threshold=2000/s` for short window.
Carla Mendes: did a flame after toggling batch_size->32 on a canary — exporter CPU dropped ~45% and p99 latency dropped ~90ms. patch diff: ```- prefetch.batch_size: 128
+ prefetch.batch_size: 32
  prefetch.window_ms: 2000```
Alex Nguyen: nice. what's the cost on throughput? any tail loss?
Carla Mendes: throughput per node down ~10%, but overall latency improved. no spans dropped (we're still within ingress quota).
Samir Patel: long-term we probably want adaptive batch sizing: start small under high concurrency, grow when backlog predictable. also expose prefetch queue depth and drain_time on the console dashboards for rollout UX.
Riya Kapoor: adding two dashboard tiles: `prefetch.queue_depth` and `exporter.drain_time_p99`. Also add alert: `drain_time_p99 > 100ms` for 5m.
Alex Nguyen: quick rollback plan: rollback the prefetcher flag via config release to previous `batch_size=32` canary -> full. Or use rollout UI to revert. Which is faster?
deploy-bot: Rollout note: v3.14.0-configmap updated 09:08 -> rollout status: 60% (canary) 09:15. Use `deploy rollback v3.14.0-configmap` to revert.
Samir Patel: rollback via rollout UI is fine; do canary first then full if green. I'll prepare a short playbook.
Ben Ortiz: action items:
- Samir: prepare canary rollback and add adaptive-batch proposal (owner: Samir)
- Riya: dashboard tiles + drain_time alert (owner: Riya)
- Carla: follow-up perf tests for proto vs json serialization and record alloc profiles (owner: Carla)
- Alex: coordinate customer-impact comms and validate no data loss (owner: Alex)
Alex Nguyen: copying @oncall and engaging SRE to watch during rollback. thanks all :thumbsup:
Riya Kapoor: I also recommend tuning route quotas temporarily for the noisy client set to limit span fanout while we stabilize. small PR incoming.
Alex Nguyen: I'll kick the rollback now and report in 10m.
Carla Mendes: post-rollback quick perf: cpu p99 back to baseline, drain_time p99 down to 22ms, p99 export latency back ~normal. leaving notes on the incident channel.
Alex Nguyen: closing thread — will follow up with a short postmortem and propose adaptive batching + new dashboard tiles. :white_check_mark:
